# AlternatingPermutations

*The up-down permutations of $[n]$: $a_1 < a_2 > a_3 < a_4 > \cdots$.*

## Usage

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\operatorname{AlternatingPermutations}(n)$ | all up-down (zigzag) permutations of $[n]$ |
| $\operatorname{At}(\operatorname{AlternatingPermutations}(n),\ i)$ | the alternating permutation at 1-based position $i$ |

## Details

- **Arity:** 1 — the ground size $n$.
- **Element:** a permutation (one-line) with strict ascents and descents alternating from the first step up: `[1, 4, 2, 3]` has $1 < 4 > 2 < 3$.
- **Result type:** `collection` of `list<integer>`, each of length $n$.
- **Count:** the Euler zigzag (secant-tangent) numbers (OEIS [A000111](https://oeis.org/A000111): $1, 1, 1, 2, 5, 16, 61, \dots$), summed from the Entringer triangle (`AlternatingPermutationCount`).
- **Order:** Entringer recursion on the first value $a_1 = k$: the tail is a down-up permutation of the rest, mapped via the complement $x \mapsto n-x$ to an up-down permutation of $[n-1]$ (`AlternatingPermutationUnrank`/`Rank`).
- **Random access:** $O(n^2)$ — each level rebuilds the Entringer row (prefix sums of the previous row).
- **Convention:** the walk starts with an ascent (up-down); the reverse-first (down-up) class is its mirror image and not a separate head.

## Examples

$\operatorname{Count}(\operatorname{AlternatingPermutations}(4)) = 5$

The 5 up-down permutations of $[4]$ in rank order are $[1, 4, 2, 3], [1, 3, 2, 4], [2, 4, 1, 3], [2, 3, 1, 4], [3, 4, 1, 2]$ — e.g. $[1, 4, 2, 3]$ reads $1 < 4 > 2 < 3$.
